gap: No result ChatGPT got states how wide each extender's glass is against a 13-inch laptop's lid: a 13.3-inch 16:9 panel is 11.59 in wide, 0.38 in inside a MacBook Air 13's 11.97 in lid, while a 14.1-inch 16:9 panel is 12.29 in, 0.32 in past it before any bezel.
standout_why: Compared against iTechGuides (cited in both chats) and LBD Software (cited in chat 1). iTechGuides only says the Duex Plus DS "suits smaller 13- to 14-inch laptops" and gives no width, weight or wattage for it. LBD Software says "a 15.6-inch panel on a 13-inch laptop hangs over the edge" and that its picks are "rated around 10 to 15 watts", but computes no overhang, weight share or battery hours. TechPP (cited in chat 2) returned HTTP 403, so it was not compared. The score is 2, not 3, because the finding confirms ChatGPT's pick and because the candidates' own body widths, weights and wattages could not be opened today.
decides: It confirms the 13.3-inch Mobile Pixels Duex Plus DS as the single-screen pick for a 13-inch laptop: 13.3 in is the largest common 16:9 size whose glass stays inside a MacBook Air 13 lid. The 14.1-inch Duex Max DS we already link overhangs on glass alone, so it is the step-up row, not the winner. The Duex Plus DS is the 13.3-inch variant of the same mobilepixels.us product (cj:mobilepixels), so the pick is linkable once a record is added. The FOPO S7 (14-inch 16:10, 11.87 in of glass) sits closer to the lid width than the FOPO S1 (14-inch 16:9, 12.20 in). FOPO's stated fit range for the S1 and S7 still has to be read before either counts as a 13-inch row.

findings.label: Reference 13-inch laptop: MacBook Air 13-inch (M4, 2025)
findings.value: 11.97 in wide, 2.7 lb, 53.8 Wh battery, up to 15 hours wireless web, drives up to two external displays
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (13-inch, M4, 2025) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's own figures. These are the laptop-side inputs for every derived figure below. The two-display limit means a dual-screen extender on native video needs this generation; base M1, M2 and M3 Airs drive one.

findings.label: Glass width against a MacBook Air 13 lid
findings.value: 11.59 in of glass, 0.38 in narrower than the 11.97 in lid
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (13-inch, M4, 2025) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: 13.3 × 16/√(16²+9²) = 13.3 × 0.8716 = 11.59 in; 11.97 − 11.59 = 0.38 in. The 13.3-inch diagonal is Mobile Pixels' figure from its store listing; 16:9 follows from 1920×1080. This is active glass only: the housing is wider, and its width was not read.

findings.label: Glass width against a MacBook Air 13 lid
findings.value: 12.29 in of glass, 0.32 in wider than the 11.97 in lid before bezel
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (13-inch, M4, 2025) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: 14.1 × 0.8716 = 12.29 in; 12.29 − 11.97 = 0.32 in. Diagonal and 16:9 are from the Dealectric record for this product (read 2026-11-21). iTechGuides places this model on "laptops roughly 14" or larger".

findings.label: 12.5-inch 16:9 panel (the size of the Trio 12.5 and SideTrak Swivel 12.5 that ChatGPT showed) against a MacBook Air 13 lid
findings.value: 10.89 in of glass, 1.08 in narrower than the 11.97 in lid
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (13-inch, M4, 2025) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: 12.5 × 0.8716 = 10.89 in; 11.97 − 10.89 = 1.08 in. The 12.5-inch diagonal comes from ChatGPT's cards, not from a maker page opened today.

findings.label: Per-screen glass width against a MacBook Air 13 lid
findings.value: S1 (14-inch 16:9): 12.20 in, 0.23 in wider than the lid; S7 (14-inch 16:10): 11.87 in, 0.10 in narrower
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (13-inch, M4, 2025) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: S1: 14 × 0.8716 = 12.20 in. S7: 14 × 16/√(16²+10²) = 14 × 0.8480 = 11.87 in. Diagonals and aspect ratios are from the Dealectric records (read 2026-11-18). Both add two screens that flank the laptop, so this is per screen.

findings.label: Battery hours a bus-powered screen costs a MacBook Air 13
findings.value: about 4.0 hours of web use at a 10 W screen and 2.9 hours at 15 W, against Apple's 15 hours with no screen
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extenders of 2026 - LBD Software
findings.note: Apple's 53.8 Wh ÷ 15 h = 3.59 W average laptop draw. 53.8 ÷ (3.59 + 10) = 3.96 h; 53.8 ÷ (3.59 + 15) = 2.89 h. The 10 to 15 W range is LBD Software's FAQ figure for its own picks ("rated around 10 to 15 watts"), not a maker figure for our candidates. Apple inputs: https://support.apple.com/en-us/122209.

findings.label: Extender weight as a share of a 2.7 lb MacBook Air 13
findings.value: ChatGPT's "under 1.5 lb" ceiling is 56% of the laptop's weight; LBD Software's top pick, the 2.29 lb KEFEYA S1, is 85%
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extenders of 2026 - LBD Software
findings.note: 1.5 ÷ 2.7 = 0.56; 2.29 ÷ 2.7 = 0.85. The 2.29 lb figure is LBD Software's; the 2.7 lb figure is Apple's. LBD Software says the KEFEYA "puts about a kilogram on your laptop lid" but does not give the share.

findings.product: Mobile Pixels Duex DS Series (Duex Plus DS 13.3-inch and Duex Max DS 14.1-inch)
findings.label: Maker's US store price and video path
findings.value: from $183.99 (list $299.99), in stock; USB-C and Mini HDMI "without the need for drivers or software"

The Max DS is $215.99 in the Dealectric record, so $183.99 is presumably the 13.3-inch Plus DS, but the variant list returned HTTP 429 and this was not confirmed per variant. Mobile Pixels' prices move with timed sales.

findings.label: What the cited rivals say about 13-inch fit
findings.value: iTechGuides: the Duex Plus DS "suits smaller 13- to 14-inch laptops". LBD Software: "a 15.6-inch panel on a 13-inch laptop hangs over the edge"
findings.source_title: 15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026: USB-C, Portable & Triple-Screen Picks
findings.note: Neither page gives a width, an overhang figure, a weight share or battery hours. The iTechGuides read covered the first 100,000 of 103,904 characters. The LBD Software quote is from https://www.lbdsoftware.com/best-laptop-screen-extenders/.

unsourced: Mobile Pixels Duex Plus DS and Duex Max DS body width, weight, power draw and stated laptop fit range: mobilepixels.us returned HTTP 429 on every product-page read, and B&H, Adorama and Lenovo returned 403.
